_README: The registry is the part of the treasury module that CANNOT be automated, and the
reason it is a file rather than code is §15: each claim must be classified
treasury-attributed, operating, recourse, non-recourse or ambiguous, and no XBRL
element carries that classification. Code inferring it from element names would be
guessing, and a wrong guess produces a net NAV that is precisely wrong instead of
honestly uncertain.
EVERY claim entry must carry a `source`: the accession number and the statement or
note it was read from. An entry without one is not evidence, and the module reports
any claim it cannot classify rather than quietly leaving it out - because omitting a
claim understates the claims and flatters NAV.
`attribution` values:
treasury   proceeds funded digital-asset purchases, or the instrument is secured on them
operating  funded the operating business; not netted against treasury NAV
ambiguous  genuinely arguable. Netted in the LOW bound only, so the band shows the
size of the disagreement instead of hiding it behind one number
CIKs below are PLACEHOLDERS marked null. Fill each from
https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json before the first run. They are left
null deliberately: a wrong CIK returns another company's facts and every downstream
figure would be confidently wrong.
Claims are likewise EMPTY, not guessed. An empty claims list makes net NAV equal
gross NAV, which for a leveraged treasury company is materially wrong - so populate
them from the filings before publishing anything. The module surfaces this.

CIKs filled 11 September 2026 from the SEC ticker file and checked against the registrant title each one returns. Claims remain empty: until they are populated the module reports gross NAV, and says so, rather than a net NAV that quietly equals it.

companies.name: Strategy Inc
companies.note: Reports under us-gaap:CryptoAssetNumberOfUnits with unit 'Bitcoin' and a null label. Verified working in btc-data. Heavily financed: convertibles and several preferred series, so the claims list below is the difference between a real net NAV and a headline gross one.

companies.name: BitMine Immersion Technologies, Inc.
companies.note: Ether-primary treasury. Confirm which tokens are tagged and with which XBRL unit string before trusting the split; a multi-token balance sheet is separated here by the unit name alone.
companies.token_declaration_source: BMNR tags us-gaap:CryptoAssetNumberOfUnits with the generic units "Integer" and "cryptoAsset", which do not name the asset, and companyfacts flattens away the dimensional member that would. The token is declared here as ETH and CHECKED: 5,700,049 units against a reported CryptoAssetFairValue of $10,871,934,000 at 2026-05-31 implies $1,907 a unit. That is ether. Against bitcoin it would be out by 98%. The reconciliation runs on every row, so the declaration is a checkable claim rather than an assumption.

companies.name: Twenty One Capital, Inc.
companies.note: Formed via SPAC. Point-in-time history begins at the business combination, not at the SPAC's listing: treat pre-combination periods as a different issuer and do not carry a series across the break.

claims.instrument: Convertible long-term notes (arrived with the 8 December 2025 business combination)
claims.source: 0001213900-26-037460, 10-K for 2025-12-31, and 2 later 10-Qs (carrying amounts). Attribution evidence: 0001213900-25-120736, 8-K filed 11 December 2025, which records that the business combination with Cantor Equity Partners, Tether Investments and iFinex closed on 8 December 2025.
claims.note: MARKED AMBIGUOUS ON THE EVIDENCE, NOT AS A FALLBACK. The notes first appear on the 2025-12-31 balance sheet, weeks after the combination closed on 8 December 2025, so they arrived through the transaction structure rather than from a standalone offering by the operating company. There is therefore no use-of-proceeds sentence of the usual kind to read: the question is what the notes funded within the combination, and that is described in the S-4 filed 17 October 2025, which has not been read. Until it is, treasury-attribution is arguable in both directions and the band is the honest answer. TO NARROW IT: read the transaction structure and pro-forma balance sheet in the S-4. If the notes financed the bitcoin contributed at closing, this becomes treasury; if they financed other consideration, operating.

companies.name: Strive, Inc.
companies.note: Confirm the correct filing entity and CIK after the merger; the ticker has changed hands.
companies.status_note: NO CRYPTO FACTS IN XBRL. A full scan of companyfacts on 11 September 2026 returned no concept matching crypto, bitcoin, ether or digital - not a unit count, not even a USD carrying value. Either no post-merger period has been filed yet, or holdings are not tagged. This is recorded as unobtainable rather than left looking like a miss: a silent zero reads as "holds no crypto", and that is the failure that excludes a real holder while looking like a fact. Re-check after the next 10-Q.

companies.name: American Bitcoin Corp.
companies.note: Miner AND treasury holder. §19: mined inventory awaiting sale is not the same economic claim as a held treasury, and counting both is a double count. Decide the treatment, record it here, and apply it consistently.

companies.name: Metaplanet Inc.
companies.note:
THREE traps here, all of which produce confident wrong numbers.
1. A sponsored LEVEL I ADR creates no SEC reporting obligation. Level I relies on the Rule 12g3-2(b) exemption: the issuer publishes its home-market disclosures in English instead of filing. Only Level II and III, which list on an exchange, file Form 20-F. So MPJPY will NOT appear in companyfacts and this issuer stays source: manual.
2. A CIK may nonetheless EXIST, because the depositary files Form F-6 to register the ADR facility. Finding a CIK is therefore not evidence that financial facts are available: companyfacts would be empty or carry only the facility. Do not read a CIK as a green light.
3. THE ADR RATIO. Per-share figures computed on the ADR count are wrong by the ratio against figures computed on the ordinary count. BTC per share, NAV per share and mNAV are all affected. Record the ratio from the deposit agreement before any per-share figure is calculated, and state which security each one is on.
Section 6 duplicate rule: the primary security is the Tokyo listing. MPJPY, MTPLF and DN3.F are the same economic exposure and must never be counted alongside it.

other_quotations.MPJPY: sponsored Level I ADR, US OTC, from 19 December 2025, depositary Deutsche Bank
other_quotations.MTPLF: unsponsored OTC quotation, superseded by MPJPY

companies.name: CleanSpark, Inc.

xbrl_mis_tag.actual_source: CleanSpark August 2026 Operational Update, 8 September 2026: bitcoin holdings were 13,703 in total as of 31 August 2026.
xbrl_mis_tag.note: The XBRL unit count is wrong by a factor of about 125. It is tagged under the standard element with the unit string 'Bitcoin', so nothing about the tag itself looks irregular: an index taking the field at face value would have valued this position near $100bn and weighted it above Strategy. The reconciliation against the filer's own CryptoAssetFairValue is what catches it, and it is the reason that check now runs on STATED tokens and not only inferred ones.

encumbrance.note: 3,951 of 13,703 is posted as collateral or recorded as receivable, all related to derivative transactions. §15 requires restrictions and encumbrances to be documented: encumbered coins are not unencumbered treasury, and a treasury index that counts them at par overstates the position. Not yet netted - the treatment has to be decided and applied consistently across every miner that posts collateral, not just the one where it was noticed.

companies.note: Mines AND holds. Two open questions before this is used: the mis-tagged unit count above, and whether mined inventory awaiting sale is the same economic claim as a held treasury (§19).

_claim_example.note: Prospectus states net proceeds were used to acquire bitcoin. `from` is the FILING or issuance date, never the period end: the claim is not knowable before it is disclosed.
